decision.explanation: A linear transformation scales area by the absolute value of its determinant. Here, |det(T)| = |7(-1)| = 7. Since the unit square has area 1, its image has area 7.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
The unit square $D$ has vertices $(1,0),(0,0),(0,1),(1,1).$ What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $T$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}7 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14074295/assets/3cbf4ce4422e043cedb73e9b10bba11e9cb1e64352ff182eff8aaa0046c4e8f3.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=1\cdot 1=1.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=7\cdot (-1)-0\cdot 0=-7.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|-7|\cdot 1 \\  & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
